This photograph Q 2978 comes from the collections of the Imperial War Museums.
hero.source: NLS Haig - Troops moving up at eventide - men of a Yorkshire regiment on the march (cropped)
hero.description: Five soldiers silhouetted against the sky. Rays of sun burst through dark clouds to create a dramatic and atmospheric shot. They are all wearing steel helmets, and three of them are clearly carrying rifles and backpacks.Original reads: 'BATTLE OF BROODSEYNDE [sic] RIDGE. - TROOPS MOVING UP AT EVENTIDE. MEN OF A YORKSHIRE REGIMENT ON THE MARCH.'The Imperial War Museum caption (Q 2978) gives "A silhouetted file of men of the 8th Battalion, East Yorkshire Regiment going up to the line near Frezenberg.")

gallery.filename: NLS Haig - Anti-aircraft gun in action during the battle.jpg
gallery.title: File:NLS Haig - Anti-aircraft gun in action during the battle.jpg
gallery.description:
Soldiers silhouetted against the sky. They are preparing to fire an anti-aircraft gun. On the right of the photograph a soldier is being handed a large shell for the gun.
OFFICIAL PHOTOGRAPHS TAKEN ON THE BRITISH WESTERN FRONT. BATTLE OF BROODSEYNDE [sic] RIDGE. Anti-aircraft gun in action during the battle. (Silhouette taken near Frezenberg).

Comment : This shows a 13 pounder 9 cwt anti-aircraft gun.

gallery.description: A ration party of the Royal Irish Rifles in a communication trench during the Battle of the Somme.  The date is believed to be 1 July 1916, the first day on the Somme, and the unit is possibly the 1st Battalion, Royal Irish Rifles (25th Brigade, 8th Division).
